candidate.educational_objective: Verify that a client considering a randomized phase 3 cancer treatment trial understands random assignment, the role of standard-treatment comparison, and the continuing voluntary right to withdraw after consent.

options.A: I may receive either the investigational treatment or the standard treatment because assignment is by chance, and I can still choose to leave the study later.
options.B: Because this is phase 3, I am guaranteed to receive the investigational treatment if I sign the consent form.
options.C: If I am assigned to the standard-treatment group, I will receive no active cancer treatment because the comparison group is always untreated.
options.D: Once I sign the consent form, I must remain in the trial until the study ends even if I later change my mind.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. NCI states that phase 3 treatment trials compare an investigational treatment with the current standard treatment. In randomized trials, assignment is by chance; neither the participant nor the doctor chooses the treatment group. NCI informed-consent guidance also states that research participation is voluntary and that a participant may leave the study after signing the consent form. B is incorrect because enrollment does not guarantee assignment to the investigational arm. C is incorrect because, in the basic cancer-treatment trial design described by NCI, the control group receives standard treatment rather than no treatment; NCI also notes that placebos are rarely used in cancer treatment trials and are not routinely substituted for effective standard therapy. D is incorrect because signing the consent form does not surrender the participant's right to withdraw.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Phase 3 cancer treatment trials compare investigational and standard treatment; randomization assigns participants by chance rather than participant/physician choice; cancer treatment trials generally preserve active standard treatment in the comparison structure; informed consent is voluntary and participants retain the right to withdraw.
